title: AI-Driven Discovery of Entanglement Witness in Spin Hamiltonians
summary: A Transformer-based entanglement classifier applied to spin-Hamiltonian states revealed a finite-temperature decision boundary that tracked the Jordan–Wigner excitation gap. Across XY, XXZ, frustrated J1–J2 and random-local Hamiltonians, the study reported strong classification against certified labels; results are numerical and theoretical, not experimental.
ai_technology: EntNet uses Transformer learning on 16 distilled local-unitary-invariant channels derived from two- to four-site Pauli correlators to classify many-body spin states as entangled or separable.
organization: University of Cambridge; University of Oxford

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: The study used synthetic states with separability labels and entanglement certificates, held out higher-order certificate classes, tested transfer across Hamiltonian families and checked 2,000 classically correlated separable states.
evidence.unknown: Numerical classification and model-based phase interpretation; no experimental system or separate-team replication was reported.
evidence.ai_role: EntNet uses Transformer learning on 16 distilled local-unitary-invariant channels derived from two- to four-site Pauli correlators to classify many-body spin states as entangled or separable.
